verification_report.summary:
The entire supplement is correct conditional on chapter_gauduchon_variational_volume.tex (independent audit gauduchon_variational_volume_01) and the expressly accepted manuscript inputs. All new deductions were checked in textual order, with no critical errors or gaps.

The normalized smooth equation and scalar uniqueness identify exactly the range over all smooth strictly positive probability measures with the range of smooth strictly positive Monge--Ampere masses. Exact-background decreasing regularization and bounded Bedford--Taylor continuity give convergence of total masses. For each fixed approximant, (1-delta)u_j preserves strict positivity and its mass converges polynomially; choosing delta separately for each j avoids any uniform estimate. Consequently both extrema agree with the usual bounded-potential v_- and v_+, allowing an infinite supremum.

Commuting the two infima is valid. With the prerequisite's exact definition of D_mu, Holder gives its maximum (integral gamma^n)^((n-1)/n), attained at mu=gamma^n/integral gamma^n. This proves the stated volume-normalized Gauduchon trace formula. Volume-one normalization yields the asserted equivalence concerning positivity, without proving PVP.

Attainment is equivalent in the two minimization problems. An attaining Gauduchon metric gives a strictly positive value and a density whose smooth solution globally minimizes mass. Dual equality and proportional volume forms make the solution a constant multiple of that Gauduchon metric. Conversely, every smooth strict global minimizer admits two-sided variations; raw-mass first variation forces the Gauduchon condition, and Stokes proves attainment of the trace quotient. Gauduchon stationarity alone is not claimed sufficient for global minimality.

On all pseudoeffective smooth backgrounds, distributional Stokes gives nonnegative numerators, so the same Holder computation proves lambda_*=inf_mu lambda_mu, including zero numerators. A fixed Gauduchon test gives finiteness; the infimum of linear functionals gives concavity and positive homogeneity, and Stokes gives smooth ddc invariance. For nef backgrounds each test quotient is A_gamma+epsilon B_gamma with B_gamma>0. Commuting the epsilon and metric infima proves the decreasing limit. At every positive epsilon it equals v_-(omega_epsilon)^(1/n) for any smooth Hermitian representative. All dimension-one cases hold with denominators one and masses equal to integral omega. No BMP, uniform bound over densities, or arbitrary singular-class lower-volume identification is used. Internal references match the accepted inputs; no new external-paper reference requires verification.
